goal: Replace the global one-live-lease-per-reviewer rule in the reviewer allocator with a tunable per-reviewer concurrency cap. Declare MAX_REVIEWER_CONCURRENCY = 3 beside MAX_AUTHOR_LANES, give each reviewer that many lease slots with slot 1 keeping the historical ref name, keep exact-object locks, exact-head pinning and the two-distinct-reviewers rule for the two slots on one pull request head unchanged, and make the refusal name the cap it hit together with each reviewer that reached it and the issue/PR pairs it holds.
prohibited_actions: No migration is authored or applied; this is repository maintenance and touches no database object
No preview or production apply, no workflow dispatch, no lane-manager mutation run, no worktree reaper run
No merge of this pull request by the worker, and never gh pr merge --admin
Do not weaken, skip, edit or disable any workflow, guard script or required check
Do not relax the same-head distinctness rule, the exact-object lock or the exact-head pin while raising concurrency
No licensed or private licensor data in any file, commit message or issue comment; this repository is public
assumptions: The single-lease rule is ours, not a provider constraint: each review already runs in its own detached worktree at its own pinned head with its own session name and its own durable verdict ref, so two concurrent reviews by one provider share no mutable state.
Independence is bought by the same-head distinctness rule, not by the global one-lease rule, so raising per-reviewer concurrency does not weaken any review guarantee.
The cap is a named constant beside MAX_AUTHOR_LANES so it is tunable without touching allocation logic; 3 is the value issue #2693 was implemented at.
Slot 1 keeps the historical lease ref name, so every lease already live under the old one-slot scheme stays readable and releasable without a migration of refs.
Provider quota is out of scope: raising concurrency does not create credit, and a reviewer that is out of quota is still unavailable.
This pull request touches no database object, so db_reads and db_writes are empty and no claim, migration version or sidecar is involved.
stop_conditions: A required check proves a real defect in the allocator change
Clearing any check would require weakening a guard, a workflow or a required check
The change would relax the two-distinct-reviewers rule on one head, the exact-object lock or the exact-head pin
The pull request base moves so that the reported files_changed no longer matches Git
